title: Beta enablement: staged rollouts for 2 pilot Dedicated customers (feature flag + learnings)
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Goal
Enable Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) for 2 pilot enterprise customers behind a feature flag / allowlist, run at least one controlled staged rollout per customer, and capture learnings + required follow-ups before GA.

Context
Dedicated tenants have strict isolation and SLA expectations. We’re shipping staged rollouts (multi-stage weights + gates + approvals) to reduce risk of pool-wide regressions. Beta needs to validate the full operator workflow end-to-end (Console + APIs + evaluator + routing + audit events), and to prove we can run safely without saturating reserved pools.

Scope (this ticket)
1) Beta customer selection + enablement coordination
- Confirm 2 pilot Dedicated customers with CS + Product (Rachel Kim + Lauren Bishop).
- Validate prerequisites per customer: pool IDs, tenant IDs, routing mode, gate metrics availability (queue depth/utilization/5xx/latency), who will approve rollouts (RBAC).
- Schedule rollout windows and comms plan (customer + internal oncall).

2) Feature flag allowlisting and rollout plan setup
- Add tenant allowlist entries for beta customers to enable Dedicated staged rollouts UI/API.
- Create initial RolloutPlan(s) for each customer (or validate customer-provided plan) with conservative stage weights:
  - Stage 0 (internal): 0% customer traffic, optional shadow if supported
  - Stage 1: 5% for 30–60 min evaluation window
  - Stage 2: 25% for 60 min
  - Stage 3: 100%
- Gates: recommended defaults from SRE (latency p95, 5xx, timeouts, queue depth, GPU utilization) with fail-safe behavior on missing/late metrics (pause/hold).

3) Operational readiness for beta
- Verify dashboards exist and oncall can triage:
  - Gate evaluator health (lag, success rate)
  - Per-pool rollout stage status panel
  - Alerts for paused/stuck rollouts
- Confirm runbook coverage for:
  - rollout paused due to failing gate
  - rollout paused due to missing metrics
  - rollback/abort behavior and expected routing outcomes
- Confirm support escalation path and handoff notes (Dev Patel / Support rotation).

4) Execute beta rollouts + capture learnings
- Run at least one staged rollout per customer (model version OR runtime config) with manual approval at each stage.
- Capture:
  - Gate false positives/negatives, metrics freshness issues, evaluator lag
  - Operator UX issues (Console status mismatches, approval latency)
  - Routing determinism checks (allocation stable under retries)
  - Capacity headroom issues at partial weights (queue depth excursions)
- Produce a short beta write-up and create follow-up tickets for:
  - required fixes before GA
  - “nice-to-have” improvements

Out of scope
- Broad customer self-serve (beta is operator-led / enterprise opt-in).
- Multi-armed bandit experimentation.

Beta entry criteria (must be true before enabling customers)
- Control plane objects + CRUD are deployed and stable (create/update/approve/abort/status).
- Gate evaluator is deployed with fail-safe hold behavior when degraded.
- Routing weight enforcement for Dedicated pools is live and tested (no cross-tenant interference).
- Audit events emitted for create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold with export pipeline working.
- Dashboards and alerts are available to SRE.

Beta exit criteria (definition of done)
- Two pilot customers enabled via allowlist.
- At least one staged rollout executed end-to-end per customer OR a documented reason why not (e.g., customer change freeze) with reschedule.
- No Sev-0/Sev-1 customer incidents attributed to the beta feature.
- Post-beta summary posted in #eng-releases / Confluence link with:
  - what worked
  - what broke / confused operators
  - concrete GA blockers and owners

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: evaluator lag causes delayed holds → mitigation: alert on evaluator lag; enforce “no auto-advance” when evaluator degraded; manual approvals required.
- Risk: missing metrics pauses rollouts indefinitely → mitigation: metrics freshness surfaced in UI; runbook includes how to validate telemetry pipeline; conservative default windows.
- Risk: partial traffic shifts saturate reserved pool due to headroom assumptions → mitigation: autoscaling/headroom guardrails enabled; start with low weights and longer windows.

Primary owners / collaborators

- Eng execution / enablement: Chloe Martin (Console backend), Mina Haddad (routing), Logan Wright (telemetry), Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- Product sign-off: Lauren Bishop / Marissa Cole

Also recommend default evaluation windows >= 30m for Stage 1 to reduce flakiness from transient spikes. Please ensure the UI surfaces metrics freshness; otherwise oncall will have a hard time distinguishing real regressions from telemetry lag.
